Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. # Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation via Tongyi's `z-image-turbo`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2511.22699v5
    * With this smaller model to generate in-progress previews: 
      * https://huggingface.co/madebyollin/taef1
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

content.content:
1	# API — the models behind one HTTP server
2	
3	`cmd/serve` is the long-lived process: an OpenAI-shaped API over the models in
4	this repository, with one flag per vertical deciding what is resident.
5	
6	    go run ./cmd/serve -llm -tts -stt
7	
8	`GOALS.md`'s last line — "we will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these
9	features, in Go" — is what this is. It is stage one of that: the routing
10	layer, three of the five verticals wired to it, and the shape the other two
11	plug into.
12	
13	## What answers today
14	
15	| Endpoint | State |
16	|---|---|
17	| `GET /v1/models` | **done** — lists what the process actually loaded, with the speech model's voices |
18	| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **done** — qwen3.8-flash-next, `-llm`, buffered and SSE |
19	| `POST /v1/responses` | **done** — the same generation, OpenAI's newer envelope |
20	| `POST /v1/messages` | **done** — the same generation, Anthropic's envelope |
21	| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **done** — kokoro, `-tts` |
22	| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **done** — parakeet, `-stt`, with word and segment timings |
23	| `POST /v1/embeddings` | 501 — `models/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` has not been started |
24	| `POST /v1/images/generations`, `/edits` | 501 — `zimage/pipeline` runs, it is not wired here |
25	
26	Every endpoint is *routed*, including the ones that are not implemented: a
27	client gets a 501 that says what is missing and, where a flag would have fixed
28	it, which flag. A 404 would mean a misspelled path and nothing else.
29	
30	## The three packages
31	
32	    cmd/serve   flags, load order, graceful shutdown
33	    backend/    the adapters: weights, device residency, one lock each
34	    api/        routing, request shapes, encoding; imports no model
35	
36	The direction of the dependency is `cmd/serve -> backend -> api`, never the
37	other way. `api` *declares* the backend interfaces (`api.SpeechBackend`,
38	`api.TranscriptionBackend`, `api.CompletionBackend`) and implements none of
39	them, so it pulls in no checkpoint loader and no Vulkan, and its tests run
40	against fakes in milliseconds — `go test ./api/` needs no `models/` directory
41	and no GPU, including for the three chat envelopes and their streams.
42	
43	What crosses the boundary is deliberately model-shaped and not
44	container-shaped. A speech backend returns `*audio.Clip` — samples and a rate
45	— and the HTTP layer encodes the WAV or the raw PCM, because which one was
46	asked for is the request's business and not the model's. A transcription
47	backend is handed an already-decoded clip for the same reason in reverse.
48	
49	**The completion backend's signature is a streaming one**, and the buffered
50	response is written in terms of it rather than the other way round. A token
51	on this part costs ~44 ms of the wall clock at 22.7 tok/s, so a 500-token
52	answer is 22 seconds: an interface that returned the whole thing would make
53	the streamed endpoint impossible to build on top of it, where the buffered one
54	is a string builder over the streaming one. That is also what keeps the two
55	answers to the same prompt identical — a server whose streaming path is a
56	separate implementation is a server whose two answers eventually differ, over
57	some whitespace one of them strips.
58	
59	## The log does not keep the conversations
60	
61	`-log-bodies` is off by default, and that default is the point: this server's
62	request and response bodies are its users' prompts and answers, and a process
63	that stays up would otherwise write every one of them to disk as a side effect
64	of having an access log. With it off the log still carries the method, the
65	path, the status, the duration and the sizes — which is what an operator reads
66	anyway. An event stream is never kept whatever the flag says: the first
67	kilobyte of one is a fragment of a frame.
68	
69	## Requests are serialised at the queue
70	
71	A `vk.Device` holds a single queue and nothing in `vk` is externally
72	synchronised, so two requests recording and submitting at once is undefined
73	behaviour rather than contention. `backend.Device` is the device plus the lock
74	that fixes that: every run and every staging pass goes through `Do`, and the
75	server is concurrent at the HTTP layer and serial at the GPU.
76	
77	That is also the only arrangement that makes sense on this part. These models
78	are each sized to saturate the iGPU; two of them interleaved would not go
79	faster, they would share a 236 GB/s bus.
80	
81	## Residency, and the one place it is not resident yet
82	
83	**The language model is resident, and it is most of the machine.** `-llm`
84	stages all 48 layers, the dense banks and the 512-expert bank at startup —
85	**33.5 s**, and the process then holds ~84 GB — so a request is a prefill and
86	one forward pass per token with no weight ever moving again. Two numbers are
87	decided at startup rather than per request: `-llm-ctx`, the attention cache's
88	cell count and so the longest conversation the process can hold, and
89	`-llm-batch`, how many tokens the prefill arenas hold. A conversation past the
90	cache is refused with both numbers rather than truncated at one end; a prompt
91	past the batch is prefilled in chunks of it, which is the same computation by
92	L7b's gate.
93	
94	**The device lock is taken per forward pass and not per request.** A
95	completion is seconds long and the speech models are milliseconds, so holding
96	the queue for a whole generation would make a transcription wait behind it for
97	nothing: between two decode steps there is no work in flight. What is held for
98	the length of a request is the *graph*, whose cache, PLE ring and DeltaNet
99	state are one sequence's — two conversations interleaved in them would not be
100	slower, they would be one conversation.
101	
102	**Parakeet is resident.** `-stt` stages the encoder and the transducer tail
103	once, sized for `-max-audio` seconds (60 by default), and every shorter clip
104	runs in the same arenas — `UploadMel` settles the geometry per run. A request
105	costs a front end on the host and two submits. A longer clip is refused with a
106	message saying what the server was sized for, rather than being truncated.
107	
108	**Kokoro is not.** Its arenas are sized for one utterance's frame count, and
109	the durations decide that, so nothing can be staged until the phoneme side has
110	run (SPEECH.md T2, T4c). `-tts-gpu` therefore stages *per request* — the
111	sequence `cmd/tts` uses, unchanged, because it is the one T4 and T6 measured —
112	and it is **off by default** until that cost is measured against the host
113	path, which is what `-tts` alone runs.
114	
115	Two things would fix it, and both are measurements rather than arguments:
116	
117	- **Bucketed residency.** Size the arenas above the utterance and zero-pad the
118	  alignment up to them, trimming the tail by `Prosody.Samples`. The phoneme
119	  side already accepts any frame count up to the one it was built for
120	  (`GPUPhonemes.sharedGraph`); whether the generator's stages tolerate the
121	  padding is the open question.
122	- **Skipping the second prosody pass.** The vocoder still reads `asr`, `f0`
123	  and `energy` from the host (SPEECH.md T7), so the host prosody that settles
124	  the length could feed the device vocoder directly and the phoneme side would
125	  not need staging at all.
126	
127	## Flags
128	
129	    -addr        127.0.0.1:8080   loopback by default
130	    -token       …                bearer token; empty serves without authorization
131	    -gpu         true             use the device where an adapter has a resident path
132	    -max-upload  128              largest body carrying a file, in MB
133	    -log-bodies  false            print request and response bodies in the access log
134	
135	    -llm             false        load qwen3.8-flash-next
136	    -llm-model       models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/…-00001-of-00004.gguf
137	    -llm-ctx         4096         cache cells: the longest conversation, prompt plus completion
138	    -llm-batch       512          tokens the prefill arenas hold
139	    -llm-max-tokens  1024         what a request that names no max_tokens gets
140	    -llm-layers      0            stage the first N layers only; a fast start, not an answer
141	
142	    -tts         false            load Kokoro-82M
143	    -tts-model   models/Kokoro-82M
144	    -tts-gpu     false            stage per utterance; see above
145	    -lexicon     models/misaki    empty takes phonemes only
146	    -espeak      true             espeak-ng for words outside the lexicon
147	    -british     false            en-GB lexicon and fallback
148	    -voice       af_heart         what a request that names none gets
149	    -noise       0                excitation noise seed; 0 leaves it off
150	
151	    -stt         false            load parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
152	    -stt-model   models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
153	    -max-audio   60               longest clip the arenas are sized for, in seconds
154	
155	## A second turn is a continuation
156	
157	A chat client re-sends the whole conversation every turn, so the naive server
158	prefills ten turns of history to answer the tenth. This one does not: the
159	adapter keeps the token sequence the graph is holding, and when a request
160	continues it — the same tokens, plus more — the new tokens are `Extend`ed onto
161	the state that is already there. That is the same call a generated token
162	makes, and L7b's gate is that a sequence in chunks is the sequence whole.
163	
164	Measured on the second turn of a two-turn conversation: **90 prompt tokens, 71
165	of them reused, 216 ms against 421**. The log says which, per request.
166	
167	The reuse is all-or-nothing, and the reason is the gated DeltaNet. A
168	divergence part way through would mean rewinding to the fork — and the
169	attention cache is masked by position and both convolution rings are addressed
170	by it, so those would survive, but a DeltaNet layer's recurrent state is a
171	running product with no inverse. So the prefix has to be the whole of what is
172	held, or the sequence starts again. A miss costs one comparison; a hit costs
173	nothing and saves the history.
174	
175	It also means **the graph is one conversation's**. Two clients are served
176	correctly — the second waits, and re-prefills — but they take turns evicting
177	each other's prefix, which is the first thing a cache per conversation would
178	fix.
179	
180	## One prompt, three envelopes, and a template that is not ours
181	
182	The three chat endpoints are one generation. `/v1/chat/completions` is
183	OpenAI's, `/v1/responses` is OpenAI's newer one, `/v1/messages` is
184	Anthropic's, and each is a translation into the same `api.CompletionRequest`
185	and back out of the same token stream. Nothing but the envelope differs, which
186	is why the tests for two of them are about the translation and not about the
187	model.
188	
189	They do disagree about **reasoning**, and usefully. A chat completion carries
190	it in a `reasoning_content` field beside the content — not OpenAI's field, but
191	the one every client that talks to a reasoning model already reads. A response
192	carries it as an *item of its own*, before the message it led to. A message
193	carries it as a `thinking` block. All three come from the same place: this
194	checkpoint's generation prompt opens a `<think>` block, so the model's first
195	token is inside it, and `llm.ChatDecoder` splits the stream at `</think>` —
196	holding back any tail that could still be the start of a marker, so a `<` at
197	the end of a token is never forwarded as an answer and then taken back.
198	
199	**The prompt itself is a transcription and not a design.** A chat request is a
200	list of messages and the model reads one string, and what turns one into the
201	other is `tokenizer.chat_template` in the GGUF's own metadata: 180 lines of
202	Jinja that merge the leading system turns, add a reasoning-effort sentence,
203	write the tool block, keep each assistant turn's `<think>`, and open the
204	generation prompt. A server that improvises that produces a prompt the model
205	has never been shown — which does not fail, it answers slightly wrong,
206	everywhere, with nothing to point at. So `llm.RenderChat` reproduces it, and
207	the acceptance criterion is Jinja's own output: `reference/dump_chat_template.py`
208	renders the template out of the checkpoint with the environment transformers
209	builds, and `TestRenderChat` diffs 23 cases character for character. The cases
210	that made it worth doing are the small ones — Python's `json.dumps` writes a
211	space after every separator where Go's encoder writes none, and escapes
212	neither `<` nor `&` where Go escapes both, so the tool block was four
213	differences away from being someone else's prompt.
214	
215	**A stop sequence is another marker.** The same holdback that keeps
216	`</think>` from being forwarded half-written keeps the first character of a
217	stop sequence out of the stream, so a streamed answer and a buffered one are
218	the same string — the sequence itself appears in neither. They are watched in
219	the *answer* and not in the reasoning, because a `stop` of `"\n\n"` would
220	otherwise end every generation inside its own working. OpenAI's envelopes fold
221	this into `finish_reason: "stop"`; Anthropic's reports `stop_sequence` and
222	says which one matched, and so does this.
223	
224	**Tool calls are read back through the schema.** The template writes a string
225	argument raw between its tags and everything else as JSON, so rebuilding
226	`arguments` needs the tool's own parameter types: `123` is the number for an
227	integer parameter and the text `"123"` for a string one. They are also the one
228	thing that is not streamed — a call is not a call until it has closed, and a
229	client sent half of one would have to be told to take it back.
230	
231	## Transcripts have times in them
232	
233	Every emission the transducer makes records the encoder frame it was made at,
234	and a TDT model also predicts how many frames to skip afterwards — so a word
235	has an end as well as a beginning without a forced alignment. `verbose_json`
236	reports both granularities OpenAI defines, `srt` and `vtt` are the same
237	segments in their two containers, and `json` stays the text alone.
238	
239	Two things about them are worth stating rather than discovering. **The timings
240	are the model's own**: the duration head is approximate in a way a Viterbi
241	alignment against the audio is not, and 80 ms is the finest it can be. And
242	**Whisper's fields are absent rather than invented** — `avg_logprob`,
243	`no_speech_prob`, `compression_ratio`, `seek` and `temperature` are properties
244	of Whisper's decoder, and a number in them here would be a number a client
245	could filter on. `language` is likewise the request's or absent: this
246	checkpoint is multilingual and does not report which language it heard.
247	
248	Words are grouped by the tokenizer's own rule (SentencePiece's U+2581 marks a
249	word start) and segments are sentences, which this model can do because it
250	punctuates — a sentence end is a token rather than a guess about silence.
251	
252	## Two extensions, and three refusals
253	
254	`POST /v1/audio/speech` takes a **`"phonemes"`** field that is not OpenAI's: IPA
255	to speak directly, winning over `input`. The checkpoint's vocabulary is 178 IPA
256	symbols and the front end that reaches them is a separate model's worth of
257	rules (SPEECH.md T5), so a caller that has already done that says so instead of
258	having it guessed. It is also how the endpoint is driven without a lexicon on
259	disk. `GET /v1/models` carries a **`voices`** array on the speech model, so a
260	client does not need a second call to populate a menu.
261	
262	What is refused rather than faked:
263	
264	- **`stream: true` on speech.** Kokoro decides the whole utterance's durations
265	  before a single sample exists, so there is nothing to send early. A whole
266	  body dressed as a stream would be a lie about latency.
267	- **`stream: true` on transcription.** The decode loop emits token by token
268	  and could stream, but the 40 µs submit-and-fence per emission is 38% of it
269	  (SPEECH.md), so what that endpoint wants is the persistent kernel, not a
270	  goroutine.
271	- **Containers other than WAV, and audio formats other than wav/pcm.**
272	  `audio/` is 16-bit PCM in and out on purpose. An mp3 request gets a 400
273	  naming what the server does encode. *Transcripts* are a different question
274	  and are no longer refused: `json`, `verbose_json`, `text`, `srt` and `vtt`
275	  all answer, because the timings they need exist.
276	
277	And on the chat endpoints, the same principle with a longer list: **`n > 1`**
278	(n completions are n runs of a model sized to saturate the device), **`min_p`
279	and `repeat_penalty`** (the sampler is temperature, top_k and top_p),
280	**`response_format` and `text.format`** other than text, a **`tool_choice`**
281	that names a function, **`thinking.budget_tokens`**, and any **image content
282	block**. Every one of them is a 400 that says what the server
283	does instead. The reason is the same each time: a knob accepted and ignored is
284	worse than a refused one, because the client never learns that turning it did
285	nothing.
286	
287	## What is left
288	
289	- Embeddings, which need a model at all.
290	- **Constrained decoding**, which is the one refusal above that is a missing
291	  capability rather than a missing shape. It would close `response_format`,
292	  `text.format` and a `tool_choice` that names a function in one go.

# API — the models behind one HTTP server

`cmd/serve` is the long-lived process: an OpenAI-shaped API over the models in
this repository, with one flag per vertical deciding what is resident.

    go run ./cmd/serve -llm -tts -stt

`GOALS.md`'s last line — "we will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these
features, in Go" — is what this is. It is stage one of that: the routing
layer, three of the five verticals wired to it, and the shape the other two
plug into.

## What answers today

| Endpoint | State |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` | **done** — lists what the process actually loaded, with the speech model's voices |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **done** — qwen3.8-flash-next, `-llm`, buffered and SSE |
| `POST /v1/responses` | **done** — the same generation, OpenAI's newer envelope |
| `POST /v1/messages` | **done** — the same generation, Anthropic's envelope |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **done** — kokoro, `-tts` |
| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **done** — parakeet, `-stt`, with word and segment timings |
| `POST /v1/embeddings` | 501 — `models/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` has not been started |
| `POST /v1/images/generations`, `/edits` | 501 — `zimage/pipeline` runs, it is not wired here |

Every endpoint is *routed*, including the ones that are not implemented: a
client gets a 501 that says what is missing and, where a flag would have fixed
it, which flag. A 404 would mean a misspelled path and nothing else.

## The three packages

    cmd/serve   flags, load order, graceful shutdown
    backend/    the adapters: weights, device residency, one lock each
    api/        routing, request shapes, encoding; imports no model

The direction of the dependency is `cmd/serve -> backend -> api`, never the
other way. `api` *declares* the backend interfaces (`api.SpeechBackend`,
`api.TranscriptionBackend`, `api.CompletionBackend`) and implements none of
them, so it pulls in no checkpoint loader and no Vulkan, and its tests run
against fakes in milliseconds — `go test ./api/` needs no `models/` directory
and no GPU, including for the three chat envelopes and their streams.

What crosses the boundary is deliberately model-shaped and not
container-shaped. A speech backend returns `*audio.Clip` — samples and a rate
— and the HTTP layer encodes the WAV or the raw PCM, because which one was
asked for is the request's business and not the model's. A transcription
backend is handed an already-decoded clip for the same reason in reverse.

**The completion backend's signature is a streaming one**, and the buffered
response is written in terms of it rather than the other way round. A token
on this part costs ~44 ms of the wall clock at 22.7 tok/s, so a 500-token
answer is 22 seconds: an interface that returned the whole thing would make
the streamed endpoint impossible to build on top of it, where the buffered one
is a string builder over the streaming one. That is also what keeps the two
answers to the same prompt identical — a server whose streaming path is a
separate implementation is a server whose two answers eventually differ, over
some whitespace one of them strips.

## The log does not keep the conversations

`-log-bodies` is off by default, and that default is the point: this server's
request and response bodies are its users' prompts and answers, and a process
that stays up would otherwise write every one of them to disk as a side effect
of having an access log. With it off the log still carries the method, the
path, the status, the duration and the sizes — which is what an operator reads
anyway. An event stream is never kept whatever the flag says: the first
kilobyte of one is a fragment of a frame.

## Requests are serialised at the queue

A `vk.Device` holds a single queue and nothing in `vk` is externally
synchronised, so two requests recording and submitting at once is undefined
behaviour rather than contention. `backend.Device` is the device plus the lock
that fixes that: every run and every staging pass goes through `Do`, and the
server is concurrent at the HTTP layer and serial at the GPU.

That is also the only arrangement that makes sense on this part. These models
are each sized to saturate the iGPU; two of them interleaved would not go
faster, they would share a 236 GB/s bus.

## Residency, and the one place it is not resident yet

**The language model is resident, and it is most of the machine.** `-llm`
stages all 48 layers, the dense banks and the 512-expert bank at startup —
**33.5 s**, and the process then holds ~84 GB — so a request is a prefill and
one forward pass per token with no weight ever moving again. Two numbers are
decided at startup rather than per request: `-llm-ctx`, the attention cache's
cell count and so the longest conversation the process can hold, and
`-llm-batch`, how many tokens the prefill arenas hold. A conversation past the
cache is refused with both numbers rather than truncated at one end; a prompt
past the batch is prefilled in chunks of it, which is the same computation by
L7b's gate.

**The device lock is taken per forward pass and not per request.** A
completion is seconds long and the speech models are milliseconds, so holding
the queue for a whole generation would make a transcription wait behind it for
nothing: between two decode steps there is no work in flight. What is held for
the length of a request is the *graph*, whose cache, PLE ring and DeltaNet
state are one sequence's — two conversations interleaved in them would not be
slower, they would be one conversation.

**Parakeet is resident.** `-stt` stages the encoder and the transducer tail
once, sized for `-max-audio` seconds (60 by default), and every shorter clip
runs in the same arenas — `UploadMel` settles the geometry per run. A request
costs a front end on the host and two submits. A longer clip is refused with a
message saying what the server was sized for, rather than being truncated.

**Kokoro is not.** Its arenas are sized for one utterance's frame count, and
the durations decide that, so nothing can be staged until the phoneme side has
run (SPEECH.md T2, T4c). `-tts-gpu` therefore stages *per request* — the
sequence `cmd/tts` uses, unchanged, because it is the one T4 and T6 measured —
and it is **off by default** until that cost is measured against the host
path, which is what `-tts` alone runs.

Two things would fix it, and both are measurements rather than arguments:

- **Bucketed residency.** Size the arenas above the utterance and zero-pad the
  alignment up to them, trimming the tail by `Prosody.Samples`. The phoneme
  side already accepts any frame count up to the one it was built for
  (`GPUPhonemes.sharedGraph`); whether the generator's stages tolerate the
  padding is the open question.
- **Skipping the second prosody pass.** The vocoder still reads `asr`, `f0`
  and `energy` from the host (SPEECH.md T7), so the host prosody that settles
  the length could feed the device vocoder directly and the phoneme side would
  not need staging at all.

## Flags

    -addr        127.0.0.1:8080   loopback by default
    -token       …                bearer token; empty serves without authorization
    -gpu         true             use the device where an adapter has a resident path
    -max-upload  128              largest body carrying a file, in MB
    -log-bodies  false            print request and response bodies in the access log

    -llm             false        load qwen3.8-flash-next
    -llm-model       models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/…-00001-of-00004.gguf
    -llm-ctx         4096         cache cells: the longest conversation, prompt plus completion
    -llm-batch       512          tokens the prefill arenas hold
    -llm-max-tokens  1024         what a request that names no max_tokens gets
    -llm-layers      0            stage the first N layers only; a fast start, not an answer

    -tts         false            load Kokoro-82M
    -tts-model   models/Kokoro-82M
    -tts-gpu     false            stage per utterance; see above
    -lexicon     models/misaki    empty takes phonemes only
    -espeak      true             espeak-ng for words outside the lexicon
    -british     false            en-GB lexicon and fallback
    -voice       af_heart         what a request that names none gets
    -noise       0                excitation noise seed; 0 leaves it off

    -stt         false            load parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    -stt-model   models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    -max-audio   60               longest clip the arenas are sized for, in seconds

## A second turn is a continuation

A chat client re-sends the whole conversation every turn, so the naive server
prefills ten turns of history to answer the tenth. This one does not: the
adapter keeps the token sequence the graph is holding, and when a request
continues it — the same tokens, plus more — the new tokens are `Extend`ed onto
the state that is already there. That is the same call a generated token
makes, and L7b's gate is that a sequence in chunks is the sequence whole.

Measured on the second turn of a two-turn conversation: **90 prompt tokens, 71
of them reused, 216 ms against 421**. The log says which, per request.

The reuse is all-or-nothing, and the reason is the gated DeltaNet. A
divergence part way through would mean rewinding to the fork — and the
attention cache is masked by position and both convolution rings are addressed
by it, so those would survive, but a DeltaNet layer's recurrent state is a
running product with no inverse. So the prefix has to be the whole of what is
held, or the sequence starts again. A miss costs one comparison; a hit costs
nothing and saves the history.

It also means **the graph is one conversation's**. Two clients are served
correctly — the second waits, and re-prefills — but they take turns evicting
each other's prefix, which is the first thing a cache per conversation would
fix.

## One prompt, three envelopes, and a template that is not ours

The three chat endpoints are one generation. `/v1/chat/completions` is
OpenAI's, `/v1/responses` is OpenAI's newer one, `/v1/messages` is
Anthropic's, and each is a translation into the same `api.CompletionRequest`
and back out of the same token stream. Nothing but the envelope differs, which
is why the tests for two of them are about the translation and not about the
model.

They do disagree about **reasoning**, and usefully. A chat completion carries
it in a `reasoning_content` field beside the content — not OpenAI's field, but
the one every client that talks to a reasoning model already reads. A response
carries it as an *item of its own*, before the message it led to. A message
carries it as a `thinking` block. All three come from the same place: this
checkpoint's generation prompt opens a `<think>` block, so the model's first
token is inside it, and `llm.ChatDecoder` splits the stream at `</think>` —
holding back any tail that could still be the start of a marker, so a `<` at
the end of a token is never forwarded as an answer and then taken back.

**The prompt itself is a transcription and not a design.** A chat request is a
list of messages and the model reads one string, and what turns one into the
other is `tokenizer.chat_template` in the GGUF's own metadata: 180 lines of
Jinja that merge the leading system turns, add a reasoning-effort sentence,
write the tool block, keep each assistant turn's `<think>`, and open the
generation prompt. A server that improvises that produces a prompt the model
has never been shown — which does not fail, it answers slightly wrong,
everywhere, with nothing to point at. So `llm.RenderChat` reproduces it, and
the acceptance criterion is Jinja's own output: `reference/dump_chat_template.py`
renders the template out of the checkpoint with the environment transformers

## Two extensions, and three refusals

- **`stream: true` on speech.** Kokoro decides the whole utterance's durations

And on the chat endpoints, the same principle with a longer list: **`n > 1`**

- Embeddings, which need a model at all.
- **Constrained decoding**, which is the one refusal above that is a missing

1	package api
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"log"
8		"net/http"
9		"strconv"
10	
11		"strix-halo-vulkan/audio"
12	)
13	
14	// Backend is what every adapter has in common: the model ids it answers to.
15	// They are what GET /v1/models lists, and what a request's "model" field is
16	// matched against -- leniently, because a client configured for "tts-1" is
17	// still asking for the only voice model this process has.
18	type Backend interface {
19		Models() []Model
20	}
21	
22	// SpeechBackend synthesises speech. It returns samples rather than a file
23	// because the container is the HTTP layer's business: the same utterance is a
24	// WAV or raw PCM depending on the request's response_format, and a model
25	// should not know which was asked for.
26	type SpeechBackend interface {
27		Backend
28		// Speak turns text, or IPA phonemes, into mono PCM. The request carries
29		// the voice and the speed; a backend that cannot honour either returns
30		// an error rather than substituting one silently.
31		Speak(ctx context.Context, req *SpeechRequest) (*audio.Clip, error)
32		// Voices are the voice names Speak accepts, sorted. GET /v1/models
33		// reports them so a client can populate a menu without a second call.
34		Voices() []string
35	}
36	
37	// TranscriptionBackend turns audio into text.
38	//
39	// The clip is decoded by the HTTP layer and handed over already in the
40	// float32 form every model in this repository reads, so a backend never
41	// parses a container. It does still check the sample rate, because resampling
42	// is a signal-processing decision and silently doing it at the door would
43	// hide a client sending 44.1 kHz into a 16 kHz model.
44	type TranscriptionBackend interface {
45		Backend
46		Transcribe(ctx context.Context, clip *audio.Clip, req *TranscriptionRequest) (*TranscriptionResponse, error)
47	}
48	
49	// CompletionBackend generates text.
50	//
51	// **The signature is a streaming one**, and the buffered response is written
52	// in terms of it rather than the other way round. That is not a preference:
53	// a token on this part costs 12 ms (LLM.md L8d), so a 500-token answer is six
54	// seconds, and an interface that returned the whole thing would make the
55	// streamed endpoint impossible to build on top of it while the buffered one
56	// is trivial to build on this. emit is called once per token; an error from
57	// it -- a client that hung up -- stops the loop and comes back from Complete.
58	//
59	// What crosses this boundary is model-shaped and not HTTP-shaped: the backend
60	// says what it generated and what stopped it, and the handler decides what a
61	// `chat.completion` object looks like. Rendering the conversation into the
62	// checkpoint's own chat template is the backend's, because the template is
63	// part of the checkpoint.
64	type CompletionBackend interface {
65		Backend
66		Complete(ctx context.Context, req *CompletionRequest, emit func(Delta) error) (*CompletionResult, error)
67	}
68	
69	// CompletionResult is how a generation ended.
70	//
71	// The text is not in it. The handler has already seen every token through
72	// emit, and a backend that returned the whole answer as well would be a
73	// second copy of it that could disagree with the first.
74	type CompletionResult struct {
75		// FinishReason is "stop" -- the model emitted an end-of-generation
76		// token, or ran into a stop sequence -- "length", or "tool_calls".
77		FinishReason string
78		// StopSequence is the stop sequence that ended the generation, when one
79		// did. OpenAI's envelopes fold that into "stop" and Anthropic's reports
80		// it, which is the only reason it is carried separately.
81		StopSequence string
82		// ToolCalls are the calls the generation made, whole. They are not
83		// streamed: a call is not a call until it has closed, and its arguments
84		// are not JSON until they have been typed against the tool's schema.
85		ToolCalls []*ToolCall
86		Usage     Usage
87	}
88	
89	// EmbeddingBackend is a placeholder: it lets a process advertise a model it
90	// has loaded through GET /v1/models, and carries no method yet, because
91	// there is no embedding model in this repository to give it one (GOALS.md).
92	type EmbeddingBackend interface{ Backend }
93	
94	// ImageBackend is a placeholder; see EmbeddingBackend. `zimage/pipeline` is
95	// the right shape for one -- resident weights, Generate(prompt, seed,
96	// progress) -- but its width and height are fixed at construction, so
97	// `aspect_ratio` is a residency question rather than a parameter and the
98	// interface should not pretend otherwise.
99	type ImageBackend interface{ Backend }
100	
101	// ErrUnsupported is what a backend returns when a request is well formed but
102	// asks for something this model cannot do -- an unknown voice, a sample rate
103	// it does not take. It becomes a 400 rather than a 500, because the client
104	// can fix it.
105	var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("unsupported request")
106	
107	// errorBody is OpenAI's error envelope, which is what every client of this
108	// API already knows how to read.
109	type errorBody struct {
110		Message string `json:"message"`
111		Type    string `json:"type"`
112		Code    string `json:"code,omitempty"`
113	}
114	
115	type errorResponse struct {
116		Error errorBody `json:"error"`
117	}
118	
119	// writeError answers with OpenAI's error shape. typ is the coarse class the
120	// client switches on ("invalid_request_error", "server_error").
121	func writeError(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, typ, msg string) {
122		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
123		w.WriteHeader(status)
124		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(errorResponse{Error: errorBody{Message: msg, Type: typ}})
125	}
126	
127	// badRequest is the client's fault; serverError is ours, and is the one that
128	// gets logged, because nobody sees the response body of a 500 at 3am.
129	func badRequest(w http.ResponseWriter, msg string) {
130		writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid_request_error", msg)
131	}
132	
133	func serverError(w http.ResponseWriter, where string, err error) {
134		log.Printf("api: %s: %v", where, err)
135		writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "server_error", err.Error())
136	}
137	
138	// backendError maps a backend's error onto a status. ErrUnsupported is the
139	// client's fault; anything else is a run that went wrong.
140	func backendError(w http.ResponseWriter, where string, err error) {
141		if errors.Is(err, ErrUnsupported) {
142			badRequest(w, err.Error())
143			return
144		}
145		if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
146			// The client hung up mid-run. There is nobody to answer.
147			log.Printf("api: %s: client cancelled", where)
148			return
149		}
150		serverError(w, where, err)
151	}
152	
153	// notLoaded is the 501 an endpoint gives when the process was started without
154	// the model behind it. The message names the flag, because the answer to
155	// "why did this 501" is almost always "it was not asked for on the command
156	// line".
157	func notLoaded(w http.ResponseWriter, what, flag string) {
158		writeError(w, http.StatusNotImplemented, "not_implemented",
159			what+" is not loaded; start the server with "+flag)
160	}
161	
162	func writeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, status int, v any) {
163		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
164		w.WriteHeader(status)
165		_ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)
166	}
167	
168	// tooLarge answers 413 when err is the body cap being hit, and reports
169	// whether it did. A body over the limit is its own failure and not a
170	// malformed one: the client can retry with a shorter clip.
171	func tooLarge(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) bool {
172		var maxErr *http.MaxBytesError
173		if !errors.As(err, &maxErr) {
174			return false
175		}
176		writeError(w, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, "invalid_request_error",
177			"the request body is larger than this server's limit of "+
178				strconv.FormatInt(maxErr.Limit, 10)+" bytes")
179		return true
180	}
181	
182	// decodeJSON reads a JSON request body into v, answering the client itself if
183	// it cannot. It reports whether the handler should carry on.
184	func decodeJSON(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, v any) bool {
185		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(v); err != nil {
186			if tooLarge(w, err) {
187				return false
188			}
189			badRequest(w, "malformed JSON body: "+err.Error())
190			return false
191		}
192		return true
193	}

1	// Package api provides the HTTP API for the AI backend.
2	//
3	// It is the routing layer and nothing else. Every endpoint is answered by a
4	// backend interface this package *defines* and does not implement -- see
5	// backend.go -- so `api` imports no checkpoint loader, no model and no
6	// Vulkan, and its tests run in milliseconds against fakes. `backend/` holds
7	// the adapters that own the weights and the device; `cmd/serve` parses the
8	// flags and wires the two together.
9	//
10	// A missing backend is not a missing route. Every endpoint is always served;
11	// one whose backend is nil answers 501. That is what makes `serve -tts`
12	// without `-stt` the same binary with a smaller resident set rather than a
13	// different build, and it is what lets a client discover what this instance
14	// can do from GET /v1/models instead of from a connection error.
15	package api
16	
17	import (
18		"net/http"
19		"time"
20	
21		"strix-halo-vulkan/util"
22	)
23	
24	// Server is one instance of the API: a bearer token and whichever backends
25	// the process loaded. The zero value serves every route, asks for no token
26	// and answers 501 to everything, which is what a test that only exercises the
27	// middleware wants.
28	type Server struct {
29		// Token is the bearer token every /v1 request must carry. Empty means
30		// the API is open, which is for a loopback-only development run; it is
31		// never the default in cmd/serve.
32		Token string
33	
34		// MaxUploadBytes bounds a request body that carries a file -- an audio
35		// upload, an image to edit. Zero takes defaultMaxUpload.
36		MaxUploadBytes int64
37	
38		// LogBodies prints each request's and response's text in the access
39		// log. It is off by default because this server's bodies are
40		// conversations: a chat endpoint with body logging on writes every
41		// prompt and every answer to disk as a side effect of having a log.
42		// With it off the log still carries the method, the path, the status,
43		// the duration and the sizes.
44		LogBodies bool
45	
46		// The backends, any of which may be nil.
47		Speech        SpeechBackend
48		Transcription TranscriptionBackend
49		Completion    CompletionBackend
50		Embedding     EmbeddingBackend
51		Image         ImageBackend
52	}
53	
54	// Handler builds the mux. It is a fresh *http.ServeMux rather than
55	// http.DefaultServeMux so that two Servers -- a test's and the process's, or
56	// two tests' -- do not collide on the global one.
57	func (s *Server) Handler() http.Handler {
58		mux := http.NewServeMux()
59	
60		// No request / response, it's just headers. This is registered outside
61		// the authorization middleware on purpose: browsers never send
62		// Authorization on a preflight.
63		mux.Handle("OPTIONS /v1/", s.log(http.HandlerFunc(util.CORSPreflight)))
64	
65		// Output: ModelsResponse{}
66		mux.Handle("GET /v1/models", s.route(s.handleModels))
67	
68		// The OG completion endpoint
69		// Input: CompletionRequest{}, Output: CompletionResponse{}
70		mux.Handle("POST /v1/chat/completions", s.route(s.handleChatCompletions))
71		// OpenAI's "Responses" API
72		// Input: ResponsesRequest{}, Output: ResponsesResponse{}
73		mux.Handle("POST /v1/responses", s.route(s.handleResponses))
74		// Anthropic's "Messages" API
75		// Input: MessagesRequest{}, Output: MessagesResponse{}
76		mux.Handle("POST /v1/messages", s.route(s.handleMessages))
77	
78		// Input: EmbeddingRequest{}, Output: EmbeddingResponse{}
79		mux.Handle("POST /v1/embeddings", s.route(s.handleEmbeddings))
80	
81		// Input: SpeechRequest{}, Output: SpeechResponse{}
82		mux.Handle("POST /v1/audio/speech", s.route(s.handleSpeech))
83	
84		// Input: TranscriptionRequest{}, Output: TranscriptionResponse{}
85		mux.Handle("POST /v1/audio/transcriptions", s.route(s.handleTranscription))
86	
87		// Input: ImageGenerationRequest{}, Output: ImageGenerationResponse{}
88		mux.Handle("POST /v1/images/generations", s.route(s.handleImageGeneration))
89		// Input: ImageEditRequest{}, Output: ImageGenerationResponse{}
90		mux.Handle("POST /v1/images/edits", s.route(s.handleImageEdit))
91	
92		return mux
93	}
94	
95	// route is the middleware stack every endpoint carries, outermost first.
96	//
97	// The body limit is outside the logger on purpose: the logger reads small
98	// bodies so it can print them, and it must never be handed an unbounded one.
99	func (s *Server) route(h http.HandlerFunc) http.Handler {
100		return s.limitBody(s.log(s.authorize(addHeaders(h))))
101	}
102	
103	// log is the access log, with or without the bodies.
104	func (s *Server) log(h http.Handler) http.HandlerFunc {
105		return util.LogRequestFunc(s.LogBodies)(h)
106	}
107	
108	// limitBody caps what a request may carry. Past the cap the read fails with
109	// an *http.MaxBytesError, which the handlers turn into a 413.
110	func (s *Server) limitBody(fs http.Handler) http.HandlerFunc {
111		limit := s.MaxUploadBytes
112		if limit <= 0 {
113			limit = defaultMaxUpload
114		}
115		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
116			if r.Body != nil {
117				r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, limit)
118			}
119			fs.ServeHTTP(w, r)
120		}
121	}
122	
123	// HTTPServer wraps Handler in an http.Server with timeouts chosen for what
124	// this API actually carries.
125	//
126	// ReadHeaderTimeout is short because a stalled header is never legitimate.
127	// ReadTimeout is minutes rather than seconds because a transcription request
128	// is an audio upload. **WriteTimeout is zero**, i.e. unbounded: a response
129	// here is a model run, and a deadline on the write side would cut off a long
130	// synthesis or a streamed completion mid-token. What bounds a slow client
131	// instead is IdleTimeout between requests.
132	func (s *Server) HTTPServer(addr string) *http.Server {
133		return &http.Server{
134			Addr:              addr,
135			Handler:           s.Handler(),
136			ReadHeaderTimeout: 15 * time.Second,
137			ReadTimeout:       10 * time.Minute,
138			WriteTimeout:      0,
139			IdleTimeout:       2 * time.Minute,
140		}
141	}
142	
143	func (s *Server) authorize(fs http.Handler) http.HandlerFunc {
144		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
145			if s.Token == "" || r.Header.Get("Authorization") == "Bearer "+s.Token {
146				fs.ServeHTTP(w, r)
147				return
148			}
149	
150			w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
151			// A write that fails here is a client that hung up, which is not
152			// this process's problem: log nothing and return.
153			_, _ = w.Write([]byte("Unauthorized"))
154		}
155	}
156	
157	func addHeaders(fs http.Handler) http.HandlerFunc {
158		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
159			// Prevent clickjacking attacks
160			w.Header().Set("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")
161	
162			// Prevent MIME-type sniffing
163			w.Header().Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")
164	
165			// Enable strict HTTPS
166			w.Header().Set("Strict-Transport-Security", "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains")
167	
168			// Control permitted sources for content
169			w.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", "default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none';")
170	
171			// Prevent information leakage
172			w.Header().Set("Referrer-Policy", "no-referrer")
173	
174			// Cross-origin isolation
175			w.Header().Set("Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy", "same-origin")
176			w.Header().Set("Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy", "require-corp")
177			w.Header().Set("Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy", "same-site")
178			w.Header().Set("X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies", "none")
179	
180			// Set CORS headers (reflects the request Origin when allow-listed)
181			util.SetCORSHeaders(w, r)
182	
183			// Remove server header
184			w.Header().Del("Server")
185	
186			// Opt out of robots
187			w.Header().
188				Set("X-Robots-Tag", "noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nositelinkssearchbox, nosnippet, notranslate, noimageindex")
189	
190			// Disable caching
191			w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0")
192	
193			fs.ServeHTTP(w, r)
194		}
195	}

2	
3	import "net/http"
4	
5	// The endpoints whose models are not wired yet.
6	//
7	// They are registered rather than left off the mux so that a client gets a
8	// 501 with a message saying what is missing, instead of a 404 that looks like
9	// a misspelled path. Each one becomes a handler when its backend arrives:
10	// embeddings when there is an embedding model at all (GOALS.md), and images
11	// when `zimage`'s pipeline is wired in. The nil check each one will then
12	// carry -- "loaded, or not asked for on the command line" -- is the one the
13	// four endpoints that do answer already have.
14	
15	func (s *Server) handleEmbeddings(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
16		notImplementedYet(w, "/v1/embeddings", "an embedding model")
17	}
18	
19	func (s *Server) handleImageGeneration(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
20		notImplementedYet(w, "/v1/images/generations", "the image model")
21	}
22	
23	func (s *Server) handleImageEdit(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
24		notImplementedYet(w, "/v1/images/edits", "the image model")
25	}
26	
27	// notImplementedYet is the other 501: not "this process was started without
28	// the model" but "no flag would have loaded it", because the route is not
29	// written yet. The two are worth distinguishing, because only one of them is
30	// fixed by a restart.
31	func notImplementedYet(w http.ResponseWriter, route, what string) {
32		writeError(w, http.StatusNotImplemented, "not_implemented",
33			route+" is not implemented on this server yet: "+what+" is not wired up")
34	}

1	// Command serve is the long-lived HTTP server: the models in this repository
2	// behind an OpenAI-shaped API.
3	//
4	// What it loads is what it is told to load. Each vertical is a flag, and a
5	// vertical that was not asked for is not in memory and answers 501 with a
6	// message naming the flag that would have loaded it:
7	//
8	//	go run ./cmd/serve -tts -stt
9	//	go run ./cmd/serve -llm                         # the language model, 84 GB resident
10	//	go run ./cmd/serve -llm -llm-layers 4           # the server, in 7 GB, for the HTTP side
11	//	go run ./cmd/serve -tts -voice bm_george -addr :8080
12	//	go run ./cmd/serve -stt -max-audio 300          # five-minute clips
13	//	go run ./cmd/serve -tts -gpu=false              # the CPU reference
14	//
15	// The endpoints that answer today are GET /v1/models, POST
16	// /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/audio/speech and POST
17	// /v1/audio/transcriptions. The rest are routed and answer 501: /v1/responses
18	// and /v1/messages are the same model in two more envelopes, embeddings wait
19	// on there being an embedding model at all, and images on zimage's pipeline
20	// being wired in.
21	//
22	// Two things about the device are worth knowing before reading the timings.
23	// **Requests are serialised at the queue**, because a vk.Device has one and
24	// nothing in `vk` is externally synchronised -- the server is concurrent at
25	// the HTTP layer and serial at the GPU, which is also the only way these
26	// models make sense on a part with one 236 GB/s bus. And **-tts-gpu stages
27	// per request**: kokoro's arenas are sized for one utterance's frame count,
28	// so the device path pays a staging pass every time and is off by default
29	// until that is measured (see backend.TTS.synthesize).
30	package main
31	
32	import (
33		"context"
34		"errors"
35		"flag"
36		"fmt"
37		"log"
38		"net/http"
39		"os"
40		"os/signal"
41		"syscall"
42		"time"
43	
44		"strix-halo-vulkan/api"
45		"strix-halo-vulkan/backend"
46	)
47	
48	// defaultToken is what the API has always used. It is a flag so that a
49	// deployment can change it, and an empty one opens the server, which is only
50	// sensible on loopback.
51	const defaultToken = "womblesofwimbledon"
52	
53	// defaultLLMModel names the shard rather than the directory it is in, because
54	// that directory now holds three checkpoints -- the model, Unsloth's imatrix
55	// and the MTP draft head -- and a directory holding more than one is
56	// ambiguous rather than convenient.
57	const defaultLLMModel = "models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00004.gguf"
58	
59	func main() {
60		log.SetFlags(log.Ltime)
61		addr := flag.String("addr", "127.0.0.1:8080", "address to listen on; loopback by default")
62		token := flag.String("token", defaultToken, "bearer token; empty serves without authorization")
63		gpu := flag.Bool("gpu", true, "run the models on Vulkan where they have a resident path")
64		maxUpload := flag.Int64("max-upload", 128, "largest request body that carries a file, in MB")
65		logBodies := flag.Bool("log-bodies", false,
66			"print each request and response body in the access log; off because they are conversations")
67	
68		tts := flag.Bool("tts", false, "load Kokoro-82M and serve /v1/audio/speech")
69		ttsModel := flag.String("tts-model", "models/Kokoro-82M", "converted kokoro checkpoint directory")
70		ttsGPU := flag.Bool("tts-gpu", false, "run kokoro on the device; it stages per utterance, see the package comment")
71		lexicon := flag.String("lexicon", "models/misaki", "misaki lexicon directory; empty takes phonemes only")
72		espeak := flag.Bool("espeak", true, "use espeak-ng for words outside the lexicon")
73		british := flag.Bool("british", false, "use the en-GB lexicon and fallback")
74		voice := flag.String("voice", "af_heart", "voice a request that names none gets")
75		noise := flag.Int64("noise", 0, "seed for the vocoder's excitation noise; 0 leaves it off")
76	
77		llmOn := flag.Bool("llm", false, "load qwen3.8-flash-next and serve /v1/chat/completions")
78		llmModel := flag.String("llm-model", defaultLLMModel, "GGUF checkpoint, shard or directory")
79		llmCtx := flag.Int("llm-ctx", 4096, "cache cells: the longest conversation, prompt plus completion")
80		llmBatch := flag.Int("llm-batch", 512, "tokens the prefill arenas hold; a longer prompt is prefilled in chunks of it")
81		llmMax := flag.Int("llm-max-tokens", 1024, "tokens a request that names no max_tokens gets")
82		llmLayers := flag.Int("llm-layers", 0, "stage only the first N layers; 0 is the model, anything else is a fast start and not an answer")
83	
84		stt := flag.Bool("stt", false, "load parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 and serve /v1/audio/transcriptions")
85		sttModel := flag.String("stt-model", "models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3", "parakeet checkpoint directory")
86		maxAudio := flag.Float64("max-audio", 60, "longest clip the transcription arenas are sized for, in seconds")
87		flag.Parse()
88	
89		if !*tts && !*stt && !*llmOn {
90			log.Printf("warning: no model was asked for; every endpoint will answer 501. " +
91				"Pass -llm, -tts and/or -stt.")
92		}
93	
94		srv := &api.Server{Token: *token, MaxUploadBytes: *maxUpload << 20, LogBodies: *logBodies}
95	
96		// The device is opened once and shared. Only the models that were asked
97		// for decide whether it is needed at all: a CPU-only run should not fail
98		// on a machine without Vulkan.
99		var dev *backend.Device
100		if *gpu && (*stt || *llmOn || (*tts && *ttsGPU)) {
101			d, err := backend.OpenDevice("strix-halo-serve")
102			if err != nil {
103				log.Fatalf("opening the device: %v", err)
104			}
105			defer d.Close()
106			dev = d
107			log.Printf("device: %s", d.Name())
108		}
109	
110		if *tts {
111			start := time.Now()
112			ttsDev := dev
113			if !*ttsGPU {
114				ttsDev = nil
115			}
116			b, err := backend.NewTTS(backend.TTSOptions{
117				Model: *ttsModel, Lexicon: *lexicon, Espeak: *espeak, British: *british,
118				Voice: *voice, Device: ttsDev, Noise: *noise,
119			})
120			if err != nil {
121				log.Fatal(err)
122			}
123			defer b.Close()
124			srv.Speech = b
125			log.Printf("tts: %s, %d voices, %s, in %v", *ttsModel, len(b.Voices()),
126				where(ttsDev != nil), time.Since(start).Round(time.Millisecond))
127		}
128	
129		if *stt {
130			start := time.Now()
131			b, err := backend.NewSTT(backend.STTOptions{
132				Model: *sttModel, Device: dev, MaxSeconds: *maxAudio,
133			})
134			if err != nil {
135				log.Fatal(err)
136			}
137			defer b.Close()
138			srv.Transcription = b
139			log.Printf("stt: %s, clips to %.0f s, %s, in %v", *sttModel, *maxAudio,
140				where(dev != nil), time.Since(start).Round(time.Millisecond))
141		}
142	
143		// The language model is staged last, and on purpose: it is most of this
144		// machine's memory and tens of seconds of staging, so a mistake in a
145		// speech flag is reported before the wait rather than after it.
146		if *llmOn {
147			start := time.Now()
148			b, err := backend.NewLLM(backend.LLMOptions{
149				Model: *llmModel, Device: dev, Context: *llmCtx, Batch: *llmBatch,
150				MaxTokens: *llmMax, Layers: *llmLayers,
151			})
152			if err != nil {
153				log.Fatal(err)
154			}
155			defer b.Close()
156			srv.Completion = b
157			layers := "every layer"
158			if *llmLayers > 0 {
159				layers = fmt.Sprintf("the first %d layers only", *llmLayers)
160			}
161			log.Printf("llm: %s, %s, %d cells of context, %d-token batches, in %v",
162				*llmModel, layers, b.Context(), *llmBatch, time.Since(start).Round(time.Millisecond))
163		}
164	
165		if *token == "" {
166			log.Printf("warning: -token is empty; this server authorizes nothing")
167		}
168		if err := listen(srv, *addr); err != nil {
169			log.Fatal(err)
170		}
171	}
172	
173	func where(gpu bool) string {
174		if gpu {
175			return "on the device"
176		}
177		return "on the host"
178	}
179	
180	// listen serves until the process is interrupted, then drains.
181	//
182	// The drain matters here more than it does for a CRUD server: a request in
183	// flight owns the GPU queue, and killing the process underneath it would
184	// leave the device to the driver to clean up. Shutdown waits for the handler
185	// to finish, and the deferred backend teardown in main then runs with nothing
186	// dispatching.
187	func listen(srv *api.Server, addr string) error {
188		hs := srv.HTTPServer(addr)
189		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
190		defer stop()
191	
192		errs := make(chan error, 1)
193		go func() {
194			log.Printf("listening on http://%s", addr)
195			for _, route := range []string{
196				"/v1/models", "/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/audio/speech", "/v1/audio/transcriptions",
197			} {
198				log.Printf("  %s", route)
199			}
200			errs <- hs.ListenAndServe()
201		}()
202	
203		select {
204		case err := <-errs:
205			if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
206				return nil
207			}
208			return err
209		case <-ctx.Done():
210			log.Printf("shutting down; waiting for requests in flight")
211			shutdown, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
212			defer cancel()
213			if err := hs.Shutdown(shutdown); err != nil {
214				return fmt.Errorf("draining: %w", err)
215			}
216			return nil
217		}
218	}
